main_reasons: Material weaknesses existed at end of 2024; during 2025 the company corrected product-costing/bill-of-materials errors in its ERP with an 'inventory valuation adjustment recorded during the year' instead of restating, so a prior-period error may have been booked in the current period

Inconsistent controls conclusions: disclosure controls are called not effective, yet ICFR is called effective and the weaknesses 'remediated' in the same year. The ICFR assessment has no auditor attestation (EGC)
Inventory fell about 59% (raw materials halved) while revenue rose 136%, and gross margin fell from 66% to 56%. This fits earlier inventory overstatement or costing errors

Complex Level 3 warrant liability accounting with toxic resets and alternative cashless exercise ($14.3M liability, $12.1M converted to equity, $1.4M FV gain). Series B fair value was set 'based on subsequent settlements'

Sloppy disclosures and internal inconsistencies: PP&E gross line shows $46K, RSU vendor expense amounts don't reconcile ($78.4K vs $93K), no visible expense for officer RSUs vesting from June 2025, many blank percentages, wrong dates
CEO/Executive Chairman terminated March 27, 2026, four days before filing. New CFO joined mid-2025. Finance staff turnover
Going-concern doubt, $1.3M cash, stockholders' equity below the Nasdaq minimum, two reverse splits (1:10, 1:30), heavy dilution and insider convertible-note financing create pressure

Mitigating: about 91% of revenue is cash-settled direct-to-consumer online sales with small receivables, so revenue is hard to fabricate. The amounts at risk are small, and the audit report from a PCAOB-registered firm is clean apart from going concern
